facts.statement: Lurdusaurus was estimated to be 7 to 9 meters long and 2 meters high when on all fours, with its stomach only 70 centimeters off the ground.
facts.quote: Lurdusaurus is estimated to have been 7 - 9 m long and 2 m high when on all-fours, but its stomach would have been only 70 cm off the ground.

facts.statement: Lurdusaurus may be the first ornithischian dinosaur identified with graviportal anatomy, an adaptation for moving slowly while supporting a heavy body mass.
facts.quote: Lurdusaurus may be the first ornithischian identified with graviportal anatomy, designed for moving slowly whilst supporting a heavy body mass.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Lurdusaurus was discovered in 1965 by Philippe Taquet at the Gadoufaoua site in the Tenere desert of Niger.
facts.quote: In 1965, Philippe Taquet discovered the holotype specimen at the Gadoufaoua site of the Elrhaz Formation, in the Tenere desert of Niger.

facts.statement: The first formal description of the species was published in 1999 by Taquet and Dale Russell, who named it Lurdusaurus arenatus.
facts.quote: In 1999, Turquet and American paleontologist Dale Russell published the first formal description, naming it Lurdusaurus arenatus.

facts.statement: The genus name Lurdusaurus means "heavy lizard", derived from Latin and Greek roots referencing the enormous weight of the fossils.
facts.quote: The generic name comes from Latin lurdus "heavy" and Ancient Greek sauros "lizard", in reference to the enormous weight of the fossils.

facts.statement: Lurdusaurus lived in a forested, riverine environment alongside various dinosaurs including Elrhazosaurus, Ouranosaurus, Nigersaurus, Suchomimus, Eocarcharia, Kryptops, and Afromimus.
facts.quote: It lived in a forested, riverine environment alongside the iguanodonts Elrhazosaurus and Ouranosaurus, the sauropod Nigersaurus, an undescribed titanosaurid, the spinosaurid Suchomimus, the carcharodontosaurid Eocarcharia, the abelisaurid Kryptops, and the noasaurid Afromimus.

facts.statement: Lurdusaurus had a snout that was about 20 centimeters wide at the tip and expanded to 30 centimeters, lacking a duck-like bill like other iguanodonts.
facts.quote: The tip of the snout may have been about 20 cm wide, and expanded back to 30 cm. That is, like other iguanodonts, it did not have a duck-like bill.

facts.statement: Although no teeth were preserved, fossil evidence shows tooth sockets for 10 tooth rows within a span of 19.5 centimeters.
facts.quote: No teeth were preserved, but MNHN GDF 43G preserves the tooth sockets for 10 tooth rows within 19.5 cm.

facts.statement: Based on skull proportions, the total length of the Lurdusaurus holotype skull may have been 83.3 centimeters in life.
facts.quote: Based on the ratio between the length of the snout and the length of the rest of the skull in iguanodonts, the total length of the holotype's skull may have been 83.3 cm in life.

facts.statement: Based on limb circumferences of 29.5 centimeters for the humerus and 45.7 centimeters for the femur, Taquet and Russell estimated the holotype weighed approximately 5.5 metric tons.
facts.quote: Based on the circumferences of the limbs – 29.5 cm for the humerus and 45.7 cm for the femur – Taquet and Russell estimated that the holotype weighed approximately 5.5 MT, conspicuously heavy for an ornithopod this size.

facts.statement: The forelimbs of Lurdusaurus were approximately 60% the size of the hindlimbs.
facts.quote: The forelimbs are 60% the size of the hindlimbs.

facts.statement: The hand of Lurdusaurus featured a massive thumb spike.
facts.quote: The hand features a massive thumb spike.

facts.statement: The tibia of Lurdusaurus was incredibly short relative to the femur, measuring 77.7 centimeters compared to 91 centimeters.
facts.quote: The tibia is incredibly short relative to the femur, respectively 77.7 cm vs. 91 cm.

facts.statement: In 2008, Gregory S. Paul argued that Lurdusaurus and Lanzhousaurus are probably not closely allied due to differences in the prepubic process, though this hypothesis remains unverifiable without more complete remains.
facts.quote: In 2008, American freelance researcher Gregory S. Paul argued that because Lanzhousaurus has a much deeper prepubic process, the two genera are probably not closely allied, though such hypotheses are wholly unverifiable without more complete remains.

facts.statement: In 2012, Taquet agreed that Lurdusaurus falls outside Iguanodontidae but remained unsure of its exact relationship with other iguanodonts.
facts.quote: In 2012, Taquet agreed with Paul that it falls outside Iguanodontidae, but was also unsure how exactly Lurdusaurus relates with other iguanodonts.

facts.statement: The species Lurdusaurus arenatus was formally named by Taquet and Russell in 1999.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, Lurdusaurus arenatus, fue formalizada por Taquet y Russell en 1999

facts.statement: Fossil remains were first discovered in 1965 by Philippe Taquet in the Elrhaz Formation of the Tenere Desert in Niger.
facts.quote: En 1965, Philippe Taquet descubrió los restos de un ornitópodo en las capas de roca de la Formación Elrhaz, en el desierto de Tenere de Níger

facts.statement: The animal was informally known as "Gravisaurus tenerensis" by Chabli in 1988 before its formal description.
facts.quote: previamente, el animal fue conocido informalmente como "Gravisaurus tenerensis" por Chabli en 1988

facts.statement: The generic name means "heavy" and the specific name means "sandy," referencing the Tenere Desert.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico se deriva del latín lurdus, "pesado", mientras que el nombre específico de la especie tipo, arenatus significa "arenoso", siendo una referencia al desierto de Tenere

facts.statement: Lurdusaurus lived in the middle Cretaceous, approximately 121 to 112 million years ago, in what is now Africa.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 121 y 112 millones de años, en el Aptiense, en lo que hoy es África

facts.statement: The fossils date to the late Aptian to early Albian stages of the Early Cretaceous, about 112 million years ago.
facts.quote: data de finales del Aptiano a principios del Albiano del Cretácico temprano período, Hace aproximadamente 112 millones de años

facts.statement: The genus time range is recorded as the Albian stage, from 113.2 to 100.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (113.2 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: The type specimen was estimated to be about 2 meters high at the hips, nearly 9 meters long, and weighing 5.5 tonnes based on limb bone circumference.
facts.quote: El espécimen tipo habría sido de aproximadamente 2 metros de altura en las caderas y se estimó que se había acercado a los 9 metros de largo mientras pesaba 5,5 toneladas según la circunferencia de los huesos de sus extremidades

facts.statement: Its neck was quite long, about 1.6 meters, longer than in relatives due to having more and relatively longer cervical vertebrae.
facts.quote: Su cuello era bastante largo alrededor de 1,6 metros, más largos que en sus parientes debido a que su vértebra cervical era más numerosa y relativamente alargada

facts.statement: Its forelimbs were proportionally short and powerfully built, with hands featuring an enlarged thumb claw.
facts.quote: Sus extremidades anteriores eran proporcionalmente cortas y poderosamente construidas, al igual que sus manos que tenían una uña del pulgar agrandada

facts.statement: Its hind limbs were also massive and proportionally short, especially the lower leg.
facts.quote: sus extremidades posteriores también eran masivas y proporcionalmente cortas, especialmente la parte inferior de la pierna

facts.statement: The foot was unusually constructed because the metatarsals lacked solid contact with each other, suggesting a fleshy pad supported most of the weight.
facts.quote: el pie estaba inusualmente construido porque los metatarsianos carecían de contacto sólido entre sí sugiriendo la presencia de una almohadilla carnosa que soportaba la mayor parte del peso

facts.statement: Its thumb claws were formidable weapons capable of inflicting possibly fatal damage to a predator if struck on the neck or flank.
facts.quote: Sus garras del pulgar habrían sido armas formidables, capaces de infligir posiblemente daño fatal a un depredador si un golpe fuera dado al cuello o al flanco

facts.statement: Its low and deep torso, which prevented high-speed fleeing, likely gave it a low center of gravity, allowing it to spin suddenly in tight circles to face an attacker.
facts.quote: su torso bajo y profundo, que lo prohibía huir a grandes velocidades, le habría dado un centro de gravedad bajo, permitiendo que gire sobre repentinamente en círculos cerrados para hacer frente a un atacante

facts.statement: Paleontologist Tom Holtz has speculated that Lurdusaurus arenatus may have led an aquatic or semi-aquatic lifestyle, similar to a hippopotamus.
facts.quote: El paleontólogo Tom Holtz ha especulado que, basándose en sus proporciones corporales y manos extendidas, Lurdusaurus arenatus puede haber llevado un estilo de vida acuático o semiacuático , similar a un hipopótamo

facts.statement: The formation's stratigraphy and aquatic fauna suggest an inland fluvial environment, completely freshwater with a humid tropical climate.
facts.quote: La estratigrafía de la formación y su fauna acuática sugieren que se trataba de un ambiente fluvial interior, completamente de naturaleza de agua dulce con un clima tropical húmedo

facts.statement: The genus authority is Taquet & Russell, 1999.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Taquet & Russell, 1999

facts.statement: The synonym "Gravisaurus tenerensis" was proposed by Chabli in 1988.
facts.quote: synonyms: "Gravisaurus tenerensis" Chabli, 1988

facts.statement: The parent group of the genus is Iguanodontoidea.
facts.quote: Parent group: Iguanodontoidea

facts.statement: Gônet, Allain & Houssaye (2026) interpreted Lurdusaurus arenatus as a likely obligate quadruped.
facts.quote: Gônet, Allain & Houssaye (2026) determine probable locomotor preferences of Iguanodon bernissartensis, Ouranosaurus nigeriensis and Lurdusaurus arenatus, interpreting the studied taxa as likely obligate quadrupeds

facts.statement: Due to its unusual body plan, describers Taquet and Russell suggested it would have superficially resembled an ankylosaurian.
facts.quote: Debido a su inusual plan corporal, los descriptores Taquet y Russell sugirieron que se habrían visto superficialmente como un anquilosauriano
